hypothesis.H1: Upstream watershed/hydrologic/reservoir signals available at forecast issue time T provide statistically significant skill, beyond naive baselines, for predicting an actionable TOC or alkalinity change at the Foothills influent ~24 hours ahead (lead = 1 day).
hypothesis.H0: They do not; at 24 hours the targets are dominated by day-to-day persistence and actionable changes are not predictable from this data.

primary_endpoint.description: 24-hour change skill: level-space MAE of the best lab-known model vs the persistence baseline (y_hat(T+1) = y(T)), pooled over rolling-origin folds test2023..test2026.
supported_if_all_of: 95% moving-block bootstrap CI of skill excludes 0 (skill_lo > 0)
Diebold-Mariano (HLN-corrected, absolute-error loss) p < 0.05 vs persistence

secondary_endpoint_event_warning.description: Onset warning at lead 1: predicting entry into TOC > 3 mg/L or Alk < 60 mg/L when not in state at T, pooled over rolling-origin folds.
supported_if_all_of: Wilson 95% lower bound of onset precision > pooled onset base rate among eligible days
secondary_endpoint_event_warning.insufficiency_rule: If pooled onset count < 20 for a target, report 'insufficient evidence' for that target's event endpoint regardless of point estimates.

scenarios.primary: lab_known (day-T grab sample available at issue time); lab_blind reported alongside as the soft-sensor-only answer
scenarios.twelve_hour_note: 12-hour prediction is not testable from daily lab data; scoped out explicitly.

verdict_language.supported: both primary-endpoint criteria families met for the target
verdict_language.insufficient_evidence: criteria not testable at reasonable power (e.g., event scarcity)

notes: No shuffled splits anywhere; rolling-origin by season only.
Thresholds TOC>3, Alk<60 are Jake's operational round numbers; confirm with operators.
All claims restricted to April-December; the influent record has no Jan-Mar data.
Readings are provisional; USGS revises after publication.
